title: cuPilot: A Strategy-Coordinated Multi-agent Framework for CUDA Kernel Evolution

mechanism.domainTask: CUDA kernel evolution and performance optimization
mechanism.populationDetail: One population P contains multiple kernel-strategy individuals, with no persistent island partition or migration.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Top-kernel historical pairs are stored in an external RAG database for later task initialization, not a distinct same-task elite survivor archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Generation-level tournament elitism and kernel-strategy crossover are described, but Algorithm 1 writes P union offspring, leaving pruning of old individuals unclear.
mechanism.generationDetail: Vanilla kernel/strategy initialization is followed by selected kernel plus selected strategy crossover, then kernel revision aligned back to strategy.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Roofline position and NCU hardware utilization guide strategy prompts and enter parent tournament criteria; details of error-message handoff are not exposed.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Tournament selects kernel and strategy components separately; hardware utilization also contributes to the criterion, and the exact tournament size is not specified.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Kernel-strategy cross-product recombination uses a separately selected strategy as a semantic parent and stores cross-task historical pairs in RAG memory.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/cuPilot A Strategy-Coordinated Multi-agent Framework for CUDA Kernel Evolution.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey population text incorrectly groups cuPilot with island/migration systems; original paper describes one P. Exact old-population deletion is unclear because Algorithm 1 uses union despite prose calling the next population generational. Two models are used only across separate experiments; the strategy source is not guaranteed to be an independent code lineage.
